title: How quantum computing will break all encryption by 2030

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: If quantum computing breaks encryption by 2030, what will that mean for global security and trust in digital systems?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Current quantum computers are too error-prone, but Shor’s algorithm could break RSA by 2030 if fault-tolerant qubits scale effectively.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A world without secure encryption risks exposing private data, undermining democracy, and enabling mass surveillance by powerful entities.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Researchers are developing post-quantum cryptography, like lattice-based algorithms, which are already being tested in NIST’s standardization process.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: A future with quantum-safe encryption could foster trust, innovation, and resilience in digital infrastructure worldwide.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The race is on—between breaking old systems and building new ones—to shape a secure, equitable quantum future.

video_cue: Animated qubits interacting with encrypted data streams, transitioning to secure quantum-encrypted networks.
